Stated Claim / Post Context:
Who is Aaron Reitz? Trump DOJ prosecutor says he’s working ‘with Main Justice’ as he threatens Democrats for conducting oversight

Reitz says he is working with the Department of Justice (DOJ) in Washington in his campaign against Democrats.

Actual Article Body:
By Yunior Rivas

November 18, 2026

to see more of our voting rights news coverage when you search.

Aaron Reitz, the Trump-appointed federal prosecutor threatening Democratic lawmakers for preparing to exercise their constitutional oversight duties, once openly vowed to investigate his political opponents “into oblivion.”

Now, Reitz says he is working with Justice Department headquarters in Washington as he targets Democratic lawmakers.

“As with all of my Office’s most significant and sensitive legal matters, I work in close coordination and cooperation with Main Justice,” Reitz told Democracy Docket Wednesday.

Join 350,000 readers who rely on our daily and weekly newsletters for the latest in voting, elections and democracy.

On Wednesday, Reitz, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Texas, targeted Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), accusing him of threatening private citizens associated with President Donald Trump. Reitz demanded that Schiff preserve documents and communications related to his planned congressional investigations, citing federal criminal civil rights statutes.

Schiff became the fifth Democratic lawmaker targeted by Reitz in just over a week, joining Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), as well as Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee.

But Reitz’s increasingly aggressive campaign against congressional oversight is hardly his first foray into using the legal system against political adversaries.

Before becoming a federal prosecutor, Reitz helped lead an effort to overturn the 2020 presidential election, vowed to strip a Democratic lawmaker of his U.S. citizenship and openly described government investigations as a means of pressuring political opponents.

During a January 2026 appearance before the Montgomery County Tea Party in Texas, Reitz described his work under Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton as pursuing people he viewed as enemies of conservative values.

He then explained how he would target those opponents even when he couldn’t bring a lawsuit.

“If I couldn’t sue you, I’d investigate you into oblivion,” Reitz said, according to remarks uncovered by reporter Judd Legum.

It wasn’t an isolated comment.
